narrative.overview:
This is an instrument panel, not a media browser. The operator is watching machine work that runs for hours and committing to decisions that cannot be taken back, so the interface behaves like broadcast equipment: a dark chassis that never competes with the content, numeric readouts in monospace, semantic colors that mean one thing each, and light that appears only where something is genuinely live.

The density is deliberate and high. Posters carry the recognition load; every other surface is compressed data. Text is small because the operator is scanning many items to find the few that need action. Where the design does spend space, it spends it on the two moments that deserve deliberation: choosing an encode quality, and destroying an original.

The palette is called Ice mono and was owner-selected. It is cool, desaturated, and almost monochrome until a status needs to speak.
keyCharacteristics: Near-monochrome cool dark, with color reserved for status meaning
Monospace for every number, label, and machine string
Glow strictly as a liveness signal, behind one toggle class
High information density; small type; tight rows
Flat, tonal depth — layered surfaces rather than drop shadows
Progressive disclosure through numbered, collapsing step cards

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Each accent maps to exactly one state: blue = live, amber = undecided, jade = resolved, orchid = duplicate, red = failed or destructive. A color never borrows another's job for visual variety.

rules.name: The 4.5 Floor
rules.body: Every text token clears 4.5:1 on every surface it can land on. text-faint sits at 4.80:1 and is the darkest text permitted; anything dimmer is a border or a fill, never type.

rules.name: The Poster Supremacy Rule
rules.body: Artwork is the only saturated thing on screen. Chrome stays desaturated so 300 posters can be scanned without fatigue.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: If a value came from a file, a probe, an encoder, or a clock, it is monospace. If a person wrote it, it is the system sans. Monospace is a signal of provenance, never a costume.

rules.name: The Steady Column Rule
rules.body: Live-updating numbers are monospace and fixed-width so a changing value never shifts the layout around it.

rules.name: The Reachable Action Rule
rules.body: A list never grows so long that the controls belonging to its container leave the screen. Cap it and offer an expander.

rules.name: The Glow Means Live Rule
rules.body: A colored glow marks something happening now or the single action being urged. Never applied for emphasis or polish. Every glow lives behind the body.glow class.

rules.name: The Flat Chassis Rule
rules.body: Surfaces at rest have no shadow. If something needs to feel raised, move it one step up the surface ramp and give it a border.

rules.name: The Dim-Don't-Move Rule
rules.body: Deselected, dropped, and excluded items lose opacity, never size or position.

dos: Do keep the entire interface in one self-contained static/index.html with inline CSS and vanilla JS — no framework, no build step, no external fonts or CDNs.
Do put every machine-produced value in monospace and every human-written string in the system sans.
Do reserve glow for what is live, and keep it behind body.glow.
Do define colors as tokens in :root. There are currently zero raw hex or hsl() literals outside that block.
Do give every interactive element a visible :focus-visible ring, an accessible name, and a keyboard path.
Do state the consequence and the size before any irreversible action.
Do cap long lists and provide an expander.
donts: Don't use alert() or confirm(). Errors are toasts in a live region; confirmations are the in-page modal with dialog semantics, a focus trap, Escape, and focus restore.
Don't add a shadow to a resting surface. Move it up the surface ramp instead.
Don't let a color take on a second meaning. Amber is undecided, not warning-ish.
Don't use text-faint or dimmer for anything below 4.5:1 on the surface it lands on.
Don't animate layout properties. Transitions are limited to background and border-color at ~120ms ease-out.
Don't introduce a light theme, an icon font, gradient text, or a decorative glass/blur effect.
Don't render an unbounded list of episodes, tracks, or conflicts.
